messages.content: 你能使用lawsuit_search功能從加州的聖塔克拉拉檢索所有涉及實體“Google”的訴訟，然後再從加州的聖馬刁檢索涉及實體“Facebook”的訴訟嗎？

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Retrieve all lawsuits involving a particular entity from specified jurisdiction. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

county.description: The jurisdiction for the lawsuit search.

state.description: The state for the lawsuit search. Default is California.

message.reasoning: The user wants to use the lawsuit_search function twice: first for entity "Google" in Santa Clara County, California; second for entity "Facebook" in San Mateo County, California. We need to call the function twice. The function signature: lawsuit_search({entity: string, county: string, state?: string}). The default state is California, so we can omit state. For Santa Clara County, entity "Google". For San Mateo County, entity "Facebook". We'll produce two function calls. According to guidelines, we should output the function calls in separate messages? The instruction: "When you want to use a tool, you must do so by responding with a JSON object with the name of the function and arguments." So we need to produce a JSON object. But we have two calls. We can either chain them? Usually we can only call one function per response. But we can call one, get result, then call next. So we need to first call for Google. Then after receiving result, call for Facebook. So we need to produce first function call. Then after receiving result, produce second. So we will produce first function call.
